recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Foundation: employee, policy, audit
recommended_phases.rationale: These three modules have zero internal dependencies on other domain modules. Employee provides identity and manager relationships. Policy defines leave types, entitlements, and approval rules. Audit provides the cross-cutting audit trail required by GP-002. All three are leaf nodes in the dependency graph and must exist before any other module can be built.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — Supporting services: validation, balance, notification
recommended_phases.rationale: These modules depend only on Phase 1 modules. Validation depends on policy and employee for rule checks. Balance depends on policy (entitlements) and employee (identity). Notification depends on employee (recipient lookup). They form the second tier and are needed before the leave orchestration module can be assembled.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — Core orchestration: leave
recommended_phases.rationale: The leave module orchestrates all other modules: it validates input (validation), checks policy eligibility (policy), verifies employee status (employee), deducts/restores balances (balance), sends notifications (notification), and writes audit records (audit). It depends on every Phase 1 and Phase 2 module and cannot be built until they are complete.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries

- **Domain layer** (innermost): Models and enums — LeaveRequest, Balance, LeavePolicy, Employee, Notification, AuditLog, LeaveStatus, LeaveType, ValidationResult. No dependencies on any other layer.
- **Repository layer**: Interfaces + implementations for each domain aggregate. All database access goes through these (GP-001). Depend only on domain models and the shared db connection.
- **Service layer**: Interfaces + implementations. Depend on repository interfaces (never implementations) and on other service interfaces. The leave module's LeaveService is the orchestrator — it depends on every other service interface.
- **Controller/Routes layer** (outermost): Fastify route handlers. Depend only on service interfaces. Enforce RBAC (GP-005) and input validation (GP-003) at this boundary.

## Dependency direction (verified acyclic)

```
leave ──→ balance ──→ policy
leave ──→ balance ──→ employee
leave ──→ policy
leave ──→ employee
leave ──→ notification ──→ employee
leave ──→ audit
leave ──→ validation ──→ policy
leave ──→ validation ──→ employee
```

employee, policy, and audit are leaf modules with zero domain dependencies. balance, validation, and notification form the middle tier. leave is the sole orchestrator at the top.

## Golden Principles coverage

- **GP-001 (Repository pattern)**: Every module defines a repository interface; services call repositories, never the database directly.
- **GP-002 (Audit records)**: LeaveService calls IAuditService on every state-changing operation (submit, approve, reject, cancel).
- **GP-003 (Input validation)**: IValidationService is called at the controller boundary before any service method executes.
- **GP-004 (No sensitive data in logs)**: Audit records capture entity references, not PII; notification messages are templated.
- **GP-005 (RBAC enforcement)**: Route handlers check roles — employees can submit/cancel their own requests; managers can approve/reject team requests; HR admins can configure policies.
- **GP-006 (Error handling)**: All async service methods are wrapped in try/catch at the route level; rejected promises propagate to Fastify error handlers.

## Key design decisions

- **Balance deduction is transactional**: deductBalance and restoreBalance are called within the same database transaction as the leave status update to prevent inconsistent state.
- **Policy is the single source of truth for entitlements**: BalanceService reads entitlementDays from PolicyService when initializing or recalculating balances.
- **Notification is fire-and-forget**: LeaveService calls notification methods but does not block on delivery status; the notification module handles its own retry/queue logic.
- **Validation is a pure function layer**: IValidationService has no side effects — it returns ValidationResult objects that controllers inspect before proceeding.
